answer: We define a mechanism where identities must commit staking collateral tied to zero-knowledge verifiable delay functions across a long planning horizon. Under a subgame-perfect punishment matrix, identity multiplication strikes a strategic reef of severe slashing penalties, yielding strictly negative expected utility. This renders Byzantine behavior an unprofitable relic of inefficient networks. Consequently, the unique Nash equilibrium converges to honest play, as the opportunity cost of capital dominates any adversarial strategy.
